תרופות IV בלבד. קנדידמיה/אספרגילוזיס חודרני. מצב רפואי שולל תרומה
טיפול מקומי בפטריה שטחית (פה, עור, ווגינה). לא סיסטמי. שכיח מאוד. כנראה לא מהווה דחייה
קריפטוקוקוס מנינגיטיס / קנדידה סיסטמי. חולים מדוכאי חיסון. מצב רפואי שולל תרומה
Dapsone למניעת PCP = סמן לדיכוי חיסוני (AIDS, מושתלים). לשאול למה. Dapsone עצמו גורם המוליזה
MDR/XDR-TB = מחלה חמורה, טיפול ארוך, ניטור צמוד. הפרעות QT. המחלה קובעת — לא התרופה
פטרת עור שטחית. טיפול מקומי. לא משפיע על כשירות תרומה. שכיח מאוד (אגיספור, אגיסטן, דקטרין)
שפעת = זיהום אקוטי. דחייה סטנדרטית. לשאול: האם עדיין חולה? חום? אנטיביוטיקה נלווית?
הרפס חוזר (labialis/genital): טיפול אפיזודי קצר — כנראה כשיר אחרי סיום. פרופילקטי כרוני: לשאול למה (דיכוי חיסוני?)
CMV = סמן לדיכוי חיסוני (AIDS, מושתלים). נויטרופניה. המצב הרפואי קובע
הפטיטיס B כרוני = דחייה קבועה מתרומת דם (HBsAg+). בדיקות סרולוגיות. אם רק anti-HBs+ (חיסון) = כשיר
HCV כרוני היה דחייה קבועה. עם DAAs שיעורי ריפוי >95%. אם SVR (sustained virologic response) = ריפוי. לבדוק מדיניות MDA עדכנית לגבי HCV cured
HBV/HCV: ראה M29_04/05. לויקמיה: המחלה קובעת. Kaposi: סמן AIDS
HIV = דחייה קבועה מתרומת דם. לא משנה סוג התרופה או Viral Load. בדיקת HIV חובה בכל תרומה
PrEP = אדם HIV-שלילי בסיכון גבוה. לא HIV+. אבל: יש לבדוק האם עדיין שלילי. התנהגות בסיכון עשויה להוות דחייה בפני עצמה. מדיניות MDA?
חשיפה לדם/נוזלי גוף. לא HIV+ אך בחלון סרולוגי. לשאול: מתי הייתה החשיפה? האם סיים 28 ימים? בדיקת HIV שלילית?
COVID = זיהום אקוטי. דחייה סטנדרטית לזיהום. 5 ימי טיפול. לשאול: סיים טיפול? ללא תסמינים?
Ribavirin+INF ל-HCV הוחלף ע"י DAAs. אם עדיין בטיפול: HCV+ = דחייה. Ribavirin גורם אנמיה המוליטית — ספירות!
Mpox = זיהום ויראלי. דחייה סטנדרטית. לשאול: ללא נגעים? ללא תסמינים?

mda_criterion: GH therapy indicates underlying pituitary/growth condition; condition determines eligibility
notes: Children with GHD unlikely to donate. Adults on anti-aging GH = off-label

mda_criterion: Acromegaly or neuroendocrine tumors = chronic condition / tumor
notes: Pituitary adenoma or carcinoid = likely medical deferral

mda_criterion: Cancer diagnosis = likely deferral regardless of treatment
notes: Same for breast cancer with goserelin

mda_criterion: Chronic gynecological condition; no infection/hematologic risk from drug itself
notes: Drug is symptomatic; condition severity varies

mda_criterion: Active IVF cycle: ovarian hyperstimulation risk → temporary defer; post-treatment: standard pregnancy deferral
notes: If pregnancy achieved → pregnancy/postpartum deferral applies

mda_criterion: Prolactinoma = pituitary tumor → medical review. Excess lactation = breastfeeding → lactation deferral
notes: Cabergoline also used for Parkinson's at higher doses (see deck 08-13)

mda_criterion: Diabetes insipidus = chronic condition. Also used for von Willebrand disease / mild hemophilia A = coagulation disorder → likely deferral
notes: Enuresis (bedwetting) use = children, not donation-relevant

mda_criterion: Labor/delivery context → standard pregnancy/postpartum deferral (6 months post-delivery)
notes: Hospital drug; donor would be in postpartum period regardless

mda_criterion: Diagnostic use only (ACTH stimulation test) — single dose, no ongoing treatment
notes: The result of the test (Addison's diagnosis) matters, not the test drug

mda_criterion: Hepatorenal syndrome = severe liver failure → medical condition precludes donation
notes: Hospital ICU drug; patient population would never present for donation

mda_criterion: Stable hypothyroidism on T4 replacement = VERY COMMON in donors. Condition well-controlled = likely eligible
notes: Eltroxin is one of the most prescribed drugs in Israel. Many healthy donors take it daily. Key question: is condition stable?

mda_criterion: Active hyperthyroidism under treatment; drug indicates condition not yet resolved or controlled
similar_mechanism_drugs: All thioamides equivalent for MDA purposes
notes: Agranulocytosis risk (rare but serious) — low WBC could affect donation safety. After treatment ends and levels normalize → may be eligible

mda_criterion: Recent I-131 treatment = RADIATION source. Standard radiation deferral period applies
notes: Patient becomes radioactive temporarily. Deferral likely 3-6 months minimum. After I-131 → usually hypothyroid → transitions to M01 (levothyroxine)

ingredient_or_family: Iodide Salts / β-Blockers for thyroid storm (F03, F05)
mda_criterion: Thyroid storm = medical emergency / hospitalization → not a donation candidate
notes: Hospital drugs for acute crisis; person would not present for donation during thyroid storm

mda_criterion: Active Graves' ophthalmopathy requiring IV biologic treatment → underlying autoimmune condition + immunomodulation
notes: New drug (2020); MDA unlikely to have specific criterion yet. Biologic + autoimmune → likely defer during treatment

mda_criterion: Thyroid cancer history → cancer deferral rules apply. TSH suppression dose of T4 indicates cancer follow-up
notes: Higher T4 dose for TSH suppression (vs replacement dose) may signal cancer history

mda_criterion: Insulin use = Type 1 or advanced Type 2. Key concern: HYPOGLYCEMIA risk during/after donation (blood loss lowers glucose further)
notes: MDA criteria likely differentiate by diabetes type and control level. Insulin pump users = T1DM marker. Hypoglycemia during donation = safety risk for donor

mda_criterion: MOST COMMON oral DM drug. T2DM on metformin alone = well-controlled, low hypoglycemia risk → likely eligible
notes: Glucophage extremely prevalent in Israel. No hypoglycemia risk from drug itself. Key: is diabetes well-controlled (HbA1c)?

mda_criterion: Hypoglycemia risk (especially glyburide); blood donation could exacerbate; condition determines eligibility
notes: Higher risk than metformin. Donor should have eaten; may need glucose monitoring

mda_criterion: Diabetes treatment; condition determines. Low hypoglycemia risk. Weight loss is side effect not concern
notes: Increasingly common. Same eligibility logic as other T2DM drugs — depends on diabetes control

ingredient_or_family: GLP-1 RAs — for OBESITY only (F11, F14)
mda_criterion: Wegovy/Saxenda/Zepbound for weight loss in NON-diabetic patients. No diabetes = different eligibility question
notes: Growing population of non-diabetic users. Drug itself = no hematologic concern. Question: does MDA ask about these?

mda_criterion: Dual indication: diabetes AND heart failure/CKD (xref deck 21). For DM = condition eligibility. For HF = cardiac deferral
notes: Important to ask WHY the donor takes it — DM vs HF vs CKD. Different deferral logic

mda_criterion: All indicate Type 2 DM treatment; no direct hematologic concern from drugs; diabetes control is key
notes: Lower risk profile than insulin/sulfonylureas. Condition-based deferral, not drug-based

mda_criterion: Advanced complications may indicate poorly controlled DM or end-organ damage → medical review
notes: Donor with known complications likely has advanced disease. CKD stage affects overall eligibility
Very common among female donors; OCs likely no deferral if stable. Check MDA criteria for specific contraceptive types
Breast cancer treatment → likely permanent deferral by condition, not by drug
Infertility treatment; donor likely deferred by condition/procedure (IVF, pregnancy attempt)
Medical abortion → deferral period after procedure. Emergency contraception (ulipristal) different context
Hypogonadism replacement may be eligible; anabolic abuse/performance → likely deferral. IM injections → check needle sharing
Known deferral in some blood banks due to teratogenicity risk (pregnant woman receiving blood). Check MDA specific criteria
Deferral likely by condition (endometriosis, breast cancer) rather than by drug
Prostate cancer → likely permanent deferral by condition
Cross-ref to deck 30; used in prostate cancer + endometriosis + precocious puberty
IM injection every 3 months; check injection-related deferral + contraceptive criteria

similar_mechanism_drugs: All systemic GCs: hydrocortisone, methylprednisolone, dexamethasone, betamethasone
notes: VERY common. Key question: WHY is donor taking steroids? The underlying condition often determines eligibility more than the drug itself. Chronic high-dose → immunosuppression concern
Used in COVID-19 (2020 onward); also cerebral edema, chemotherapy antiemetic. Short courses may be eligible

similar_mechanism_drugs: All inhaled GCs: ciclesonide, mometasone, flunisolide
notes: Inhaled GCs for stable asthma = very common, minimal systemic effect. Likely eligible if asthma well-controlled
OTC topical hydrocortisone very common; minimal systemic absorption. Likely eligible unless severe skin condition
Addison's disease = chronic condition requiring lifelong replacement. Eligibility depends on disease stability
Multiple indications: HF, HTN, hirsutism, hyperaldosteronism. xref→decks 19/20/21. Eligibility depends on underlying condition
Cushing's = serious condition → likely deferral by condition. Also xref→deck 27 as antifungal (different context)
Cancer = almost always PERMANENT DEFERRAL by condition. Active chemo = absolute deferral (myelosuppression, immune compromise). This is the single most important MDA rule for this entire deck
Low-dose MTX for autoimmune conditions is DIFFERENT from cancer doses. Common in RA/psoriasis. Eligibility depends on underlying condition + immunosuppression level

similar_mechanism_drugs: All hormonal agents: letrozole, fulvestrant, exemestane + CDK4/6i
notes: IMPORTANT for MDA: Many breast cancer survivors take hormonal therapy for 5-10 YEARS after treatment. They may present as healthy donors. Need clear policy on cancer survivors + ongoing hormonal therapy
Immunotherapy can produce long-term remissions. Growing population of 'cancer-free' patients still on maintenance immunotherapy. Immune-related AEs may affect multiple organs
CML patients on imatinib can have normal life expectancy and feel healthy. They may present as donors. Lifetime oral medication. Need MDA policy clarity
Cyclophosphamide sometimes used for severe RA, SLE, vasculitis — NOT cancer. Different deferral logic than cancer use
Also used outside oncology: post-operative nausea, pregnancy nausea. If donor takes ondansetron, ask WHY — could be benign use
HF patients unlikely to donate (condition-based deferral). Narrow therapeutic index drug
IV-only drug = hospitalized patient = not a donor scenario
